title: Royal Dance Phawar of Weiking (Ka Phawar Shad Weiking)
cultural_context: The ceremonial phawar chanted at the opening and closing of the annual royal dance at the Weiking arena, from Sweetymon Rynjah's landmark 2000 monograph.

khasi: Hoi-kiw! Hoi-kiw! Risaw ko madan Weiking,
Ha ka sngi ba donburom u Hynniewtrep;
Ki Syiem, ki Myntri, ki Lyngdoh ki wan,
Ban pynkyntang ia ka shad ba kmen;
Ka tangmuri ka sawa sha ki suiñ,
Ki ksing ki nakra ki pynkhih ia ka khyndew;
Ki khun ki hajar ki kmen sngewbha,
Ban pynneh ia ka niam bad ka akor.
english: Hoi-kiw! Hoi-kiw! Ring out, O arena of Weiking,
Upon this noble day of the Seven Huts;
The Syiems, the Ministers, the High Priests arrive,
To consecrate the joyous festival dance;
The Tangmuri oboe soars into the sky,
The thunderous drums vibrate through the earth;
Preserving our sacred faith and righteous conduct.

khasi: Kupar ba kynrei U Blei Un theh,
Ha ki pynthor, ha ki kper bad ki lum;
Ban roi ka spah, ban roi ka jaid,
Ban man ka kba bad u sohkymphor;
Ai ba ka jingsuk kan shong junom,
Ha man ki tnum, ha man ki dpei,
Katba dang ieng u Lum Shillong
Ka Ri kan im ha ka hok.
english: Abundant divine favor may God pour down,
Upon valley paddies, upon orchards and mountains;
May our families prosper, may our clans multiply,
May the rice flourish and the fruit trees bend low;
May everlasting peace make its dwelling,
Beneath every thatched roof, around every hearth,
As long as Shillong Peak stands tall,
Our Motherland shall thrive in righteousness.

vocabulary.weiking: sacred grounds of the annual Shad Suk Mynsiem in Shillong
vocabulary.myntri: traditional clan cabinet minister of a Khasi Hima
